turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would see to it that their eldest son was married with all the proper ceremony and that she would be present in spirit, watching over them all. He promised her that the feast would be as she wished, with all the care and love she had always shown.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan quietly that she would ensure everything was perfect for the eldest son’s marriage, as O-lan had wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if the eldest son and the maid understood their responsibilities and if they would follow the guidance she had given them.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he understood his duties and would do his best to follow her guidance.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked her husband and son to ensure that the marriage feast was a reflection of her love and care for her family, and that it would bring happiness to all present.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and the eldest son that he would make certain the marriage feast was a celebration of O-lan’s love and care, and that it would bring joy and unity to the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would ensure the marriage feast was a true representation of his mother’s wishes and would strive to uphold her legacy.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she hoped her guidance would ensure their family's happiness and prosperity, even after she was gone.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan and the eldest son that he would oversee the preparations for the marriage feast personally, ensuring it was a grand celebration that would honour O-lan’s memory and secure their family’s future.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the maid and the eldest son should also take an active role in the preparations, ensuring that her last wishes were not only fulfilled but also remembered by future generations.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan and the eldest son that she would do everything in her power to assist with the preparations, ensuring that O-lan’s last wishes were carried out with the utmost care and respect.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would work closely with the maid to ensure the marriage preparations were perfect, reflecting his mother’s wisdom and care.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the eldest son and the maid that she wanted the marriage to be a symbol of her enduring presence, a promise to Wang Lung and their family that even in her absence, her spirit would guide them.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan and the eldest son that she would consult with the other servants to ensure that the wedding preparations were impeccable, reflecting the deep respect and love she held for O-lan.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the eldest son should personally oversee the selection of the wedding gifts, ensuring that they reflected the family's values and her own wisdom.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and the maid that he would take great care in selecting the wedding gifts, ensuring that they were a fitting tribute to her wisdom and the family’s values.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the wedding gifts should be chosen with the utmost care, reflecting not only her wisdom but also her deep love for her family and their future.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son assured O-lan and the maid that he would carefully choose gifts that would not only honor his mother’s memory but also serve as a guiding light for his wife and him in their marriage.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that the eldest son should also involve his new wife in the gift selection process, to ensure she felt included and valued as part of the family.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and the maid that he would consult with his new wife on the selection of the gifts, making sure she felt a part of the family's traditions and wisdom.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
